title: Towards Effective and Transferable Physical Camouflage against Multi-View BEV-based 3D Perception in Autonomous Driving
claim: Baseline methods leave the target detectable under the same conditions, while only ours makes the object evade detection.
layout: 8 panels, 2x4 grid, same scene, detection boxes as evidence
description: A 2x4 grid of the same rendered street scene, with one white SUV at an intersection in each panel. The panels are labeled (a) Normal, (b) AdvPatch, (c) FCA, (d) DTA, (e) ACTIVE, (f) RAUCA, (g) CNCA and (h) BEVCA. Each car carries a different texture. The textures run from plain white, to small patchy prints, to bright psychedelic and zebra-like patterns, to a muted, camouflage-like pattern in the last panel. Orange 3D bounding boxes surround the car in panels (a) to (g), which shows it is still detected. Panel (h), the proposed method, has no orange box around the car, so the detector misses it. The eye goes first to the bright cars and then to the one panel in the bottom-right where the box is missing. Captions are plain text below each panel.
caption: Comparison of 3D detection results using different textures on the photo-realistic simulation environment, where only the adversarial camouflage generated by our BEVCA framework successfully evades detection. (a) A vehicle with normal painting; (b) AdvPatch [ref]. (c)-(g) are the top-performed methods against 2D detection: FCA [ref], DTA [ref], ACTIVE [ref], RAUCA [ref], and CNCA [ref] respectively; (h) Our method BEVCA.
abstract: Modern autonomous driving systems widely adopt multi-view Bird's-Eye-View (BEV) based 3D perception models due to their superior performance. Despite their success, the robustness of these models against adversarial camouflage attacks remains largely unexplored. Existing camouflage attacks primarily target single-view 2D detectors, limiting their effectiveness in multi-view 3D perception settings. To address this gap, we propose BEVCA, a novel adversarial camouflage generation framework tailored for multi-view BEV-based 3D perception. Our framework integrates a BEV-feature-based adversarial loss with a multi-view neural rendering module, enabling effective and transferable camouflage attacks across different models and tasks. Extensive experiments in both digital and physical settings demonstrate that BEVCA outperforms state-of-the-art baselines and exhibits strong robustness under real-world conditions. Our code is available at https://github.com/WAVE-AT-IDEA/BEVCA.
